_note: Chinese festivals hub. Dates are given as lunar-calendar days (fixed) plus the usual Gregorian window, never a specific year's date. 'readings' are slugs of existing readings; 'video' is a YouTube id from content/videos.json. Written 2026-09-24.

festivals.when: 1st day of the 1st lunar month; falls between 21 January and 20 February
festivals.about: The biggest holiday of the year. Families travel home for the reunion dinner on New Year's Eve, children get red envelopes, doors get red couplets, and the celebrations run for about two weeks, up to the Lantern Festival.

festivals.when: 15th day of the 1st lunar month; the first full moon of the year, usually in February
festivals.about: The last day of the New Year celebrations. People eat sweet rice balls, hang and look at lanterns, and guess the riddles written on them.

festivals.when: one of the 24 solar terms, around 4 or 5 April
festivals.about: A day to remember ancestors: families visit and tidy graves and offer flowers. It is also a spring outing day. Because it is a day of remembrance, people do not wish each other a happy Qingming.

festivals.when: 5th day of the 5th lunar month; late May to late June
festivals.about: Remembered through the story of the poet Qu Yuan. People race dragon boats and eat zongzi, sticky rice wrapped in leaves. The usual greeting wishes health rather than happiness.
greetings: Wishing you good health this Dragon Boat Festival
words: sticky rice dumplings wrapped in leaves
Qu Yuan, the poet the festival remembers

festivals.when: 7th day of the 7th lunar month; usually in August
festivals.about: Based on the legend of the cowherd and the weaver girl, two lovers who can meet only once a year on a bridge of magpies. Today it is a day for couples.

festivals.when: 15th day of the 8th lunar month; mid-September to early October
festivals.about: The night of the fullest moon of the year and a festival of family reunion. People look at the moon, eat and give mooncakes, and tell the story of Chang'e, who lives on the moon.
words: Chang'e, the goddess of the moon

festivals.when: 1 October, followed by a week-long holiday
festivals.about: Marks the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949. The holiday week, the Golden Week, is one of the busiest travel times of the year.

festivals.when: 9th day of the 9th lunar month; usually in October
festivals.about: Traditionally a day to climb to a high place and look at chrysanthemums; today it is also a day to show respect and care for older people.
Not festivals, but the celebrations learners are most often invited to. Noodles for a long life on a birthday, red envelopes and a lot of toasting at a wedding.
